To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The total annual costs of the alcohol and tobacco problems in Estonia are approximately EUR 400 million, 2) the annual costs of alcohol problems are approximately EUR 300 million, and the annual costs of tobacco problems are approximately EUR100 million, and 3) the annual costs are approximately EUR 200 million for the health care sector, EUR 50 million for social services, EUR 100 million for the economy, and EUR 50 million as lost productivity.
The costs of alcohol and tobacco use are high, and the health effects are severe.

(a) the costs of alcohol-related mortality and morbidity in Estonia are estimated to be 2.4% of GDP; (b) the cost-effectiveness of a comprehensive package of alcohol and tobacco policies is estimated to be €1.3 per QALY; (c) the cost-effectivity of the package is highly sensitive to assumptions about the effectiveness of alcohol and tobacco interventions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the cost-effectiveness of the following alcohol and tobacco control measures in Estonia: 1) the introduction of a tax on beer, 2) the introduction of an excise tax on alcohol, 3) the introduction of graphic health warnings on cigarette packs and 4) the introduction of plain packaging for cigarettes.
the cost of smoking, the cost of smoking cessation, and the cost of smoking control.
the costs of alcohol and tobacco consumption and the costs of alcohol- and tobacco-related diseases and deaths, as well as the cost-effectiveness of different alcohol- and tobacco-control strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence to suggest that the use of e-cigarettes is associated with any significant increase in the use of tobacco cigarettes.
there are no significant health effects associated with the use of alcohol in moderation, and that there is no evidence to support a recommendation to drink in order to achieve any health benefits.
there are no significant differences between alcohol and tobacco in terms of the number of deaths caused, and the number of people who are addicted.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are working on a project to develop an alcohol and drug policy in Estonia, and we are doing this by developing a cost-effectiveness model to estimate the cost of different policy interventions.
the results of the present study indicate the need for more effective and more comprehensive interventions in the field of alcohol and tobacco prevention and control.
alcohol and tobacco control is an important part of public health in Estonia and that the cost-effectiveness of the interventions is good.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cost-effectiveness of tobacco control interventions is highly dependent on the baseline prevalence of tobacco use.
the cost-effectiveness of interventions to control alcohol and tobacco is very similar in Estonia and in the UK.
alcohol and tobacco control policies can have a significant impact on health outcomes.
